programme: SIRT1-restrained RELA/NF-κB transcription: SIRT1 deacetylates and represses RelA(p65)-driven inflammatory/survival gene expression, with ZNF148 sitting on the same p53-linked stress-arrest arm (CDKN1A, CDKN2A, TP53, plus interferon-response genes STAT1, OAS1, IFNG) that this deacetylation checkpoint also touches.
role_in_a: In Huntington's disease, SIRT1 activity (pharmacologically boosted by resveratrol in the retrieved models) is reported as neuroprotective against mutant-huntingtin/3-NP toxicity, and RelA/p65-dependent NF-κB transcription is separately reported to drive cytokine, endocannabinoid and microRNA gene programmes in HD models — the SIRT1-RelA deacetylation link is the natural bridge between these two independently retrieved findings, restraining an otherwise chronic inflammatory transcriptional output in stressed neurons/glia. ZNF148's one HD paper places it in a broader post-mortem network-analysis, consistent with a p53/stress-arrest arm but not mechanistically resolved here.
role_in_b: In clear cell renal cell carcinoma, the retrieved SIRT1 paper places it among histone-acetylation-based regulators used to define molecular subtypes, but does not resolve whether it acts to suppress or promote tumor transcription. RELA itself has no confirmed hit in the ccRCC literature retrieved; its expected relevance rests on the well-known VHL-loss/pseudohypoxic, inflammation-permissive microenvironment of ccRCC, in which NF-κB signalling is generically active — that expectation is not evidenced in this record.
shared_axis: Both diseases involve chronically stressed tissue (proteotoxic stress in HD neurons, pseudohypoxic/inflammatory stress in ccRCC) in which the amount of NF-κB(RelA)-driven transcription that escapes containment is plausibly set by SIRT1's deacetylase activity; if that checkpoint operates similarly in both tissues it would explain why the same small set of factors recurs, but no source here states the two diseases share this axis.
reasoning: SIRT1 and RELA are each independently and repeatedly placed in Huntington's disease by the retrieved literature, and their deacetylation relationship is a well-characterized biochemical module, so the programme is nameable from the factors themselves. The kidney side is thin — SIRT1 has one ambiguous ccRCC paper and RELA has none — so disease-B involvement, and the cross-disease link specifically, rests on reasoning about NF-κB/SIRT1 biology in cancer rather than on anything retrieved for this pair.
support: 42400730 - resveratrol/SIRT1 neuroprotection reviewed across HD and related neurodegenerative models; 42331250 - resveratrol via SIRT1 alleviates motor dysfunction in 3-NP-induced HD; 41186033 - bromelain-induced protection in 3-NP HD model attributed in part to SIRT1; 38784035 - SIRT1/resveratrol/aging review touching HD; 34631694 - SIRT1 among histone-acetylation regulators defining molecular subtypes in clear cell renal carcinoma, mechanism unresolved; 24360910 - NF-κB p65/RelA co-regulates cytokine and endocannabinoid genes in HD models; 25757558 - p65/RelA and p53 jointly regulate microRNA-100/146a/150 in mouse HD models; 27924190 - network analysis of post-mortem HD microarrays potentially implicating ZNF148, association uncertain.
how_to_falsify: In parallel HD neuronal/glial models and ccRCC tumor lines, activate or knock down SIRT1 and measure RelA K310 acetylation and NF-κB target-gene transcription (e.g. IL6, CCL5, BIRC3 from RELA's target list); also test whether ZNF148 knockdown changes CDKN1A/CDKN2A/STAT1 expression in the same models. If SIRT1 status does not track with RelA acetylation/activity in both tissues, or ZNF148 has no effect on the shared arrest genes, the proposed convergent module does not hold.
caveats: Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 315 patient-group comparisons, so the large supported_in counts reflect limited independent biological replication, not many unrelated studies. Blood (HD) and kidney (ccRCC) are mismatched tissues, so a checkpoint validated in one need not transfer to the other. RELB, NFKB2 and BCL3 — other NF-κB-family members — were removed as tissue-generic, meaning this account rests on RELA alone rather than a corroborated multi-subunit NF-κB signature; that could understate real NF-κB involvement rather than rule it out. The single-view exclusions (AR, BRD4, THAP1, TRIM22, etc.) show no chromatin/nuclear-receptor factor recurred broadly enough to belong in this story, and ZNF148's HD evidence is explicitly flagged as only a 'potential' link, so it should be read as the weakest of the three carrying factors.
